brief:
Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot said Sunday he will work to form a broad government as quickly as possible following a deadlocked election, Al-Monitor reported. The election failed to dislodge Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from power, leaving Eisenkot's path to leadership uncertain.

Eisenkot, a Netanyahu rival, has positioned himself as an alternative to the incumbent prime minister. The deadlock between competing political blocs has complicated efforts to form a governing coalition with a clear parliamentary majority.

title: Eisenkot seeks wide coalition after deadlocked Israeli election
